moments.title: New Year's Day
moments.angle: A Friday start, so a long weekend almost everywhere. Fresh starts sell, but January budgets are thin. Pair ambition with value.
moments.hook: New year. Same you, better plan.
moments.avoid: Resolution shaming. Anything that makes people feel behind on day one.

moments.title: New Year's Day
moments.angle: Fresh start energy, but money is tight after December. Pair aspiration with value.
moments.avoid: Heavy party or spend big content. The December hangover is financial as much as anything.

moments.title: Dry January and Veganuary
moments.angle: Alcohol free, plant based and wellness brands own the month. Retail and hospitality can play too with alternatives, not lectures.
moments.avoid: Preachy tone. Mocking people who drop out mid month.

moments.title: Day after New Year
moments.angle: Rwanda gets a second day. Family visits and slow living content.
moments.hook: Another day with the people who matter.

moments.title: Back to school
moments.angle: Lunchboxes, uniforms, school fees stress, the first drop off. Big for FMCG, banks and telcos.
moments.hook: New term, same hustle, fresh start.
moments.avoid: Assuming every family can afford the full list. Kenya opens 4 January. Uganda opens in February, so plan it separately. Confirm each ministry's term dates.

moments.title: Njaanuary season
moments.angle: The longest month. Brands that admit it and offer real value earn trust fast.
moments.avoid: Mocking people who are broke. Laugh with them, never at them.

moments.title: Zanzibar Revolution Day
moments.angle: Island pride and heritage. Institutional tone works best.
moments.avoid: Political commentary. Keep it about people and place.

moments.title: Australian Open
moments.angle: Two weeks of late night and early morning viewing across time zones. Summer in the south, sofa season in the north.
moments.avoid: Using tournament marks without rights.

moments.title: Australia Day
moments.angle: A contested date for many Australians. Brands that speak should do so with care or not at all.
moments.avoid: Flag waving promotions. Read the room in Australia this year.

moments.title: NRM Liberation Day
moments.angle: A political anniversary. Most brands should acknowledge lightly or sit it out.

moments.title: Holocaust Remembrance Day
moments.angle: International day of remembrance. Institutional messages only.
moments.avoid: Any commercial content. Pause scheduled posts in markets where the day is observed.

moments.title: Heroes' Day (Umunsi w'Intwari)
moments.angle: Honour, sacrifice, national values. Respectful institutional posts only.
moments.hook: Tribute to the heroes who built Rwanda.
moments.avoid: Sales, discounts or jokes.

moments.title: Black History Month (US and Canada)
moments.angle: Credible only with real stories, real creators and money behind it. Audiences check.
moments.hook: Celebrate the makers, not the moment.
moments.avoid: A colour swap on the logo and nothing else.

moments.title: Ncwala ceremony (Eastern Province)
moments.angle: Ngoni first fruits ceremony near Chipata. Strong heritage content for Zambian brands.
moments.hook: The first harvest belongs to everyone.
moments.avoid: Using sacred ritual imagery as a costume. Work with the organisers.

moments.title: Carnival and Mardi Gras
moments.angle: Rio, Salvador, New Orleans, Venice, Trinidad, Cologne. Colour, music, street food and joy before Lent. Mardi Gras falls on 9 February.
moments.avoid: Costume as caricature. Borrowing cultural dress you do not understand.

moments.title: Lunar New Year, Year of the Goat
moments.angle: 6 February is the day. A week of travel, family, red packets and gifting across East and South East Asia and the diaspora worldwide. The biggest human migration of the year.
moments.hook: Home is where the year begins.
moments.avoid: Mixing up zodiac animals. Assuming everyone calls it Chinese New Year; use Lunar New Year in mixed markets.

moments.title: Waitangi Day
moments.angle: New Zealand's national day. Reflective as much as celebratory.

moments.title: Ramadan
moments.angle: Expected start 8 February, moon sighting confirms. Iftar tables, generosity, night time commerce and family. Nearly two billion people adjust their days.
moments.hook: Ramadan Kareem. The table is bigger this month.
moments.avoid: Daytime food indulgence aimed at fasting audiences. Posting greetings before the official start.

moments.title: Ramadhan
moments.angle: Iftar tables, generosity, night markets on the coast. Food, telco and banking brands lead. Moon sighting sets the exact start.
moments.hook: Ramadhan Kareem. Futari ni ya familia.
moments.avoid: Daytime food indulgence content aimed at Muslim audiences. Never make fasting a joke.

moments.title: Lent
moments.angle: Ash Wednesday 10 February. Forty days of restraint for many Christians. In 2027 Lent and Ramadan overlap almost entirely, a rare shared season of discipline.
moments.avoid: Ignoring one faith's calendar in a mixed market.

moments.title: Lent (Ash Wednesday 10 Feb)
moments.angle: 2027 insight: Lent and Ramadhan run almost side by side. Two faiths fasting in the same weeks is a rare unity story.
moments.hook: Two fasts. One season. Tuko pamoja.
moments.avoid: Picking one faith's calendar and ignoring the other in the same market.

moments.title: Super Bowl LXI
moments.angle: Inglewood, California, 14 February. The biggest advertising night in the world lands on Valentine's Day for the first time. Snacks, beer, betting, streaming and the ads themselves.
moments.hook: Game night. Date night. Same night.
moments.avoid: Using league marks or the game's name in ads without rights. Say the big game.

moments.title: Valentine's Day
moments.angle: A Sunday inside both Lent and Ramadan, and Super Bowl Sunday in the United States. Love for friends, family and self works harder than candlelit clichés this year.
moments.avoid: Alienating singles. Heavy indulgence aimed at fasting audiences.

moments.title: Valentine's Day
moments.angle: Falls on a Sunday inside both Lent and Ramadhan. Love for family, friends and self works better than candlelit dinners this year.
moments.avoid: Alienating singles. Pushing indulgence to fasting audiences.

moments.title: Archbishop Janani Luwum Day
moments.angle: Faith, courage and conscience. Reflective tone.

moments.title: Lantern Festival
moments.angle: Closes the Lunar New Year period. Lanterns, sweet rice balls, reunion.

moments.title: Kuomboka ceremony (Western Province)
moments.angle: The Litunga's royal barge moves to higher ground. Date is set by the Barotse Royal Establishment when the floods are right.
moments.hook: When the water rises, a kingdom moves.
moments.avoid: Announcing a date before the royal establishment does.

moments.title: Long rains
moments.angle: Comfort food, home care, mosquito protection, planting season upcountry. Use the weather as creative terrain.

moments.title: International Women's Day
moments.angle: A public holiday in many countries. Real names, real stories, real pay data. Audiences call out empty gestures within minutes.
moments.hook: Name her. Pay her. Promote her.
moments.avoid: Pink filters and a stock quote.

moments.title: International Women's Day
moments.angle: Public holiday in Uganda and Zambia. Real stories and real names, not slogans.
moments.avoid: Pink filters and a generic quote. East African audiences call it out fast.

moments.title: Eid al Fitr
moments.angle: Expected 9 or 10 March by moon sighting. New clothes, sweets, family visits and gifting from Jakarta to London to Lagos. Keep two versions ready.
moments.avoid: Posting a day early. Wait for the announcement in each market.

moments.title: Eid al Fitr
moments.angle: Public holiday. New clothes, family lunches, coastal celebrations. Moon sighting confirms the day, so keep two versions ready.
moments.hook: Idd Mubarak. Sherehe ni ya wote.
moments.avoid: Posting the greeting a day early. Wait for the official announcement.

moments.title: Youth Day
moments.angle: Young Zambians, jobs, ambition, creativity. Telco and education brands.

moments.title: Mothering Sunday (UK and Ireland)
moments.angle: The fourth Sunday of Lent. Flowers, cards, meals. Include every kind of mother and be gentle with those grieving.
moments.hook: For the one who showed up.
moments.avoid: Assuming everyone has a mother to celebrate.

moments.title: St Patrick's Day
moments.angle: Ireland's day, celebrated loudly across the diaspora. Hospitality, drinks and green everything.
moments.avoid: Drunk stereotypes.

moments.title: Zanzibar music festival season
moments.angle: The islands host one of the continent's best loved music festivals, set for 19 to 21 March, after Ramadhan and Eid. Lifestyle, drinks and travel brands.

moments.title: Nowruz
moments.angle: Persian New Year at the spring equinox, celebrated across Iran, Afghanistan, Central Asia, the Caucasus and the diaspora. Spring cleaning, the Haft Sin table, renewal.
moments.avoid: Confusing Nowruz with Lunar New Year or with Islamic holidays.

moments.title: Holi
moments.angle: Holika Dahan bonfires on the night of 22 March, colours on 23 March in India. The festival of colours across India, Nepal and the diaspora. Joy, mess, forgiveness, spring.
moments.avoid: Colour powder imagery on white skin only. Cast the people who actually celebrate.

moments.title: Good Friday
moments.angle: Start of the Easter weekend. Reflective in the morning, road trips by afternoon.

moments.title: Holy Saturday
moments.angle: Zambia's four day Easter. Family and travel.

moments.title: Easter Sunday
moments.angle: Western Easter. Good Friday 26 March and Easter Monday 29 March are public holidays in much of Europe, Africa, Australia and the Americas. Chocolate, family lunches, spring travel.
moments.avoid: Irreverent humour on Good Friday.

moments.title: Easter Sunday and Easter Monday
moments.angle: Primary FMCG and hospitality window. Family lunches, travel upcountry and to the coast.
moments.avoid: Irreverent humour on Good Friday.

moments.title: April Fools' Day
moments.angle: High engagement for fake launches with a clear reveal by noon. Best for playful brands.
moments.hook: We launched it. Or did we?
moments.avoid: Fake health, safety or money claims. Anything that looks like a scam.

moments.title: April Fools' Day
moments.angle: High engagement for fake launches with a clear reveal. Best for fun FMCG brands.
moments.hook: We launched it. Or did we?
moments.avoid: Fake health or money claims. Anything that looks like a scam.

moments.title: Qingming (Tomb Sweeping Day)
moments.angle: Families honour ancestors across China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and the diaspora. Quiet, respectful.
moments.avoid: Promotions tied to the day.

moments.title: Karume Day
moments.angle: Remembers Zanzibar's first president. Institutional tone.

moments.title: Kwibuka 33 begins
moments.angle: Commemoration of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. A week of mourning, then 100 days of remembrance to 4 July. Only respectful institutional messages using the official theme.
moments.avoid: Any promotion, product, humour or bright colours. Pause scheduled campaigns in Rwanda this week.

moments.title: Songkran
moments.angle: Thai New Year water festival. Bangkok's streets become a water fight. Travel, drinks, sun care.
moments.avoid: Treating a spiritual new year as only a party.

moments.title: Vaisakhi
moments.angle: Sikh new year and harvest festival, also Punjabi, Tamil, Bengali and other South Asian new years fall this week.

moments.title: World Snooker Championship centenary
moments.angle: The championship turns 100, and Sheffield's Crucible hosts it for a 51st straight year. Niche but beloved in the UK, Ireland, China and beyond.

moments.title: Passover
moments.angle: Begins at sunset 21 April. Family seders, matzah, freedom stories. Late this year because 5787 is a leap year.
moments.avoid: Leavened food promotions aimed at observant audiences.

moments.title: Earth Day
moments.angle: Credible only with real action to show: numbers, suppliers, commitments. Everything else reads as greenwash.
moments.avoid: Greenwashing. A leaf on the logo.

moments.title: ANZAC Day
moments.angle: Remembrance in Australia and New Zealand. Dawn services. Respectful tone only.
moments.avoid: Sales tied to the day.

moments.title: Union Day (Muungano)
moments.angle: 63 years of Tanganyika and Zanzibar together. Unity and pride.

moments.title: Kenneth Kaunda Day
moments.angle: Legacy, unity, humility. KK's white handkerchief is an iconic cue, used with respect.
moments.avoid: Caricature.

moments.title: Golden Week (Japan)
moments.angle: A string of national holidays. Domestic travel, leisure, family.

moments.title: NFL Draft
moments.angle: Washington DC hosts for the first time since 1940. Fandom, hope, merchandise.

moments.title: International Workers' Day
moments.angle: A Saturday. Public holiday in most of the world outside North America. Celebrate the people who make things.

moments.title: Labour Day
moments.angle: Falls on a Saturday. Celebrate workers, from boda riders to nurses.

moments.title: Orthodox Easter
moments.angle: Five weeks after Western Easter this year. Greece, Russia, Ukraine, Serbia, Ethiopia, Egypt's Copts and the diaspora.
moments.avoid: Assuming Easter is over.

moments.title: Cinco de Mayo
moments.angle: Big in the United States, modest in Mexico. Food, drinks, music.
moments.avoid: Sombrero stereotypes. Confusing it with Mexican Independence Day.

moments.title: Mother's Day (most markets)
moments.angle: Second Sunday of May in the US, Canada, Australia, most of Europe, Asia and Africa. One of the biggest gifting days of the year.
moments.avoid: Assuming everyone has a mother to celebrate. Add a gentle line for those grieving.

moments.title: Mother's Day
moments.angle: Big gifting and emotion moment. Include mothers of every kind.
moments.avoid: Assuming everyone has a mother to celebrate. Add a gentle note for those grieving.

moments.title: Eid al Adha
moments.angle: Expected 16 or 17 May. Sacrifice, sharing, feeding neighbours. Public holidays across the Muslim world.
moments.avoid: Posting before moon sighting confirmation.

moments.title: Eid al Adha
moments.angle: Sacrifice, sharing, feeding neighbours. Food and FMCG sharing packs.
moments.avoid: Posting before the official moon sighting.

moments.title: French Open
moments.angle: Clay season in Paris.

moments.title: Vesak
moments.angle: 20 May in India, Singapore and most markets; a few national calendars differ, so check locally. Buddha Day across Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Korea and beyond. Lanterns, offerings, kindness.
moments.avoid: Buddha imagery as decor.

moments.title: Africa Day
moments.angle: Pan African pride across the continent and the diaspora. A public holiday in some countries.

moments.title: Africa Day
moments.angle: Public holiday in Zambia. Pan African pride builds naturally into the June football championship.

moments.title: Madaraka Day

moments.angle: Millions walk to Namugongo, some for weeks from Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. Faith, endurance, hospitality along the route. Water and FMCG sampling is common and welcome.
moments.avoid: Commercial noise inside the shrine grounds.

moments.title: Champions League final
moments.angle: Madrid, 5 June. The biggest club football night of the year.
moments.avoid: Using competition marks without rights.

moments.title: World Environment Day
moments.angle: Real action only.
moments.avoid: Greenwashing.

moments.title: World Environment Day
moments.angle: Credible only if the brand has real action to show.
moments.avoid: Greenwashing.

moments.title: Dragon Boat Festival
moments.angle: Races, rice dumplings, family across China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia.

moments.title: National Heroes' Day
moments.angle: Ordinary heroes work well: teachers, mothers, boda riders.

moments.title: Zanzibar film festival season
moments.angle: Film, art and travel audiences.
moments.avoid: Confirm the dates with the organisers. The 2026 edition ran in late June.

moments.title: Day of the African Child
moments.angle: Children's rights, education, play. Kids and education brands.

moments.title: Juneteenth
moments.angle: Freedom day in the United States. Community, history, Black owned business.
moments.avoid: Sales framing.

moments.title: Africa Cup of Nations
moments.angle: Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania host the continent's championship. Fan zones, watch parties, telco data, food and drink across Africa and the diaspora.
moments.avoid: Using the tournament's marks or name commercially without rights.

moments.angle: The continental nations championship returns to East Africa for the first time since 1976, with Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania as the first ever triple hosts. Watch parties, fan zones, nyama choma, betting, telco data, beer, FMCG multipacks. Group stage 19 to 30 June, final 17 July. Plan six months ahead.

moments.title: Father's Day (most markets)
moments.angle: Third Sunday of June in the US, UK, Canada, France, India, Japan, most of Africa. Lands inside the Women's World Cup and the Africa Cup of Nations.

moments.title: Father's Day

moments.title: FIFA Women's World Cup
moments.angle: Brazil hosts, the first time in South America. 32 teams, eight cities, final at the Maracanã on 25 July. The fastest growing audience in sport.

moments.title: Anniversary of the 2024 protests
moments.angle: A painful date for many young Kenyans. Most brands should stay quiet and pause cheerful posts.
moments.avoid: Promotional content, jokes or borrowing protest imagery.

moments.title: Wimbledon
